ads.title: Backyard Legends
ads.description: Adidas's 2026 hero spot, set in streets and side-lots and built on the idea that legends are forged in backyard games. Stars Timothée Chalamet, Lionel Messi, Bad Bunny, Lamine Yamal, Jude Bellingham and Trinity Rodman — six headliners under the 'You Got This' platform. The 90s-coded visual register is the most editorial decision in the spot. Reach extended materially by talent reposts: Chalamet and Beckham have shared the creative on their own channels.

ads.title: Get Access to FIFA World Cup 2026
ads.description: Marriott Bonvoy's 'Get Access' platform — the hospitality side of the 2026 activation, framing matchday access and Marriott Bonvoy Moments hotel stays as the path to the World Cup experience. Co-branded with Visa as payments partner. Marriott is FIFA's Official Hotel Supporter for North America (Tier 3 Regional Supporter), with the activation spanning 104 matches across the three host countries.

ads.title: Let It Pour
ads.description: Budweiser's 2026 platform film with Erling Haaland and Jürgen Klopp, built on the 'letting it all out' frame — pressure and catharsis as the emotional center, cinematic moments scaled to fan reactions worldwide. The longer hero in Bud's 2026 tournament work.

ads.title: The Most Epic Watch Party
ads.description: Lay's reactivates 'No Lay's, No Game' as its tournament platform — a fictional WhatsApp watch party where Messi, Beckham, Henry, Putellas and Steve Carell share the same group chat. The Carell casting is the spot's editorial wink. Distribution is heavily talent-amplified: Messi and Putellas both reposted the campaign to their own followers.

ads.title: Power Your Fate
ads.description: Powerade's 'Power Your Fate' platform with Lamine Yamal and Rodrygo Goes — the brand positioned as the fuel between preparation and the decisive moment. Cinematic readiness-rituals frame, distributed across global TV, digital and creator content.

ads.title: The Superior Match
ads.description: Michelob Ultra's 2026 platform under 'Superior is Worth Playing For', launched May 12 with the hotel-lobby pitch film: Pulisic, Sergiño Dest and Antonee Robinson go up against Messi, Lautaro Martínez and Nicolás Paz, with Guillermo Ochoa in goal, a Ronaldo Nazário cameo, Alex Morgan with the late assist, and Billy Bob Thornton as the lobby guest waiting on his beer. Builds on the December 2025 Superior Player of the Match trophy reveal under the same Anheuser-Busch Official Beer Sponsor activation. Christian Pulisic's own-channel repost feeds the campaign's IG distribution past Michelob's age-gated brand handle.

ads.title: Pepsi Football Nation
ads.description: Pepsi's 'Football Nation' global platform with David Beckham handing the playbook to fans — fan interactions, playful rivalry, memes and real-time reactions over match action. Featured cast also includes Vinícius Jr., Mohamed Salah, Florian Wirtz, Lauren James and Alexia Putellas. The campaign's YouTube canonical (on Pepsi Global) carries the sub-title 'The Home of Football Banter & Rivalry.' Distribution leans on talent reposts from Beckham, Vinícius Jr. and Putellas — each amplifying the spot to their own followings.

ads.title: Celebration ft. David Beckham
ads.description: Stella Artois's 'For Moments Worth More' platform with David Beckham — shared viewing occasions, hospitality and the social side of the tournament, rather than match action itself. A quieter register than the Bud line in the same AB InBev portfolio. Beckham's own Instagram repost is the campaign's primary social distribution lever.

ads.title: 50 Days to Go
ads.description: Diageo's 50-days-to-go countdown moment ahead of the June 11 opener — a portfolio-wide brand activation tying multiple Diageo labels to the tournament.

ads.title: The Coooors Call
ads.description: Coors Light's 'Coooors Call' bit — announcer Andrés Cantor stretching the elongated 'GOOOOAL' shout into the brand name. A :30 spot, with a UGC arm inviting fans to submit their own Coooors Call (featuring Cantor's son in the social cut). Beer-money prize.

ads.title: Do You Believe? Everything Can Happen on Home Soil
ads.description: FOX Sports's US broadcaster platform for 2026, anchored on the 'home soil' narrative — the first US-hosted men's tournament since 1994. Built for the broader American audience the network needs to recruit beyond core football fans. As FIFA's English-language US broadcast rights holder (104 matches across FOX and FS1, plus 4K streaming on FOX One), FOX runs licensed FIFA-branded creative.

ads.title: Copa do Mundo Brahma
ads.description: Brahma's 2026 platform film. AB InBev's flagship Brazilian beer running its own local narrative alongside Bud's global Haaland/Klopp work — more national-team coded, more Carnival-adjacent in visual register. Distribution extended via talent reposts from Ronaldo Nazário and Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti.

ads.title: When Fans Go Wild
ads.description: Motorola's 2026 global tournament film, framed around fan reactions and device-as-camera storytelling. The brand's headline 2026 activation, distinct from regional cutdown variants that surface on local channels.

ads.title: The Big Drop
ads.description: Budweiser's bottle-design platform for 2026 — a separate creative track from the main 'Let It Pour' brand spot, focused on Bud's collectible packaging and the design system across the tournament cycle. Same global activation umbrella as Let It Pour but a distinct creative concept, not a cutdown.

ads.title: JUMP (FIFA World Cup 2026 Anthem)
ads.description: Coca-Cola's official 2026 anthem — an updated cover of Van Halen's 'Jump' performed by J Balvin, Amber Mark, Steve Vai and Travis Barker. Released via Real Thing Records in partnership with Capitol Records. The standalone music drop after a teased preview in January's 'Bubbling Up' film.

ads.title: Uncanned Emotions
ads.description: The second film in Coca-Cola's 'All the Feels' trilogy (after January's 'Bubbling Up', before a third spot timed to kickoff). Focuses on raw, unfiltered fan reactions — spontaneous celebrations, disappointments, shared viewing experiences. Coke has been a FIFA stadium partner since 1950.

ads.title: Ultimate Access
ads.description: Verizon's 'Ultimate Access' platform, launched September 2025 as the brand's first World Cup activation under Official Telecommunications Sponsor status. Beckham works his way from the nosebleeds down to the pitch, anchored on the 'no one gets you closer' line. Rolled out across Sept–Dec 2025 in four waves, each released across IG + TikTok with new talent and creative — Tim Howard, Chucky Lozano, the Thompson sisters, plus the 'Golden Ticket' sweepstakes rewarding 20 customer fans with personal video calls from the all-star roster.

ads.title: The world's gone football
ads.description: Owen Trevor Black's Rattling Stick film for Lenovo, framing the brand's AI infrastructure as the engine behind the most technologically advanced World Cup in history. Shot in a Bucharest studio with AI-generated and AI-enhanced vignettes — itself a statement about where the work is going.

ads.title: The Next Legend
ads.description: Kia's 2026 hero, built around the brand's 'movement that inspires' positioning. Connects football's generational legend-making to Kia's sponsorship platform — a global, multi-generational fan story rather than a celebrity-first read.

ads.title: Home Field Advantage
ads.description: Jim Beam × U.S. Soccer co-branded launch. 'Home advantage' as the emotional center — shared viewing moments and matchday rituals at home and in local bars, not stadium reverence. Distributed across digital, social, and on-trade promotions.

ads.title: U.S. Soccer Anthem
ads.description: Boston Beer Co's 'Drink like a Believer' platform for Truly. The campaign launches a nationwide search to rename one American town 'Believe, USA', with USMNT's Weston McKennie as the anchor. Brand plans a full town takeover of the winning community ahead of kickoff.

ads.title: Bubbling Up
ads.description: The opener of Coca-Cola's 'All the Feels' trilogy, released January 27, 2026 — three months before 'Uncanned Emotions' and four months before the JUMP anthem dropped as a standalone track. A fan's pre-tournament anticipation spills into everyday moments (the elevator scene as the central creative metaphor), with a sneak preview of the JUMP anthem before its full release. The platform-launch film for Coke's broader 2026 activation.

ads.title: Everyone Wants a Piece
ads.description: Lego's tournament play stacks Messi, Ronaldo, Mbappé and Vinícius Jr. into brick-built worlds where football fandom and creative play are the same posture. The YouTube canonical lives on Lego's own channel in Short format; the real reach is built across the cross-platform social rollout — Lego's own 6 IG cuts and 6 TT posts, plus talent reposts from Messi (×2), Ronaldo and Vinícius Jr. on their own channels, which together drive the bulk of the IG view count.

ads.title: Trust What's Inside
ads.description: Gatorade's 'Trust What's Inside' platform for 2026 — performance and athlete-prep framing. PepsiCo's sports-nutrition arm running parallel to Pepsi's own banter-coded 'Football Nation' platform. Vinícius Jr.'s own-channel repost extends the campaign's IG reach beyond the brand handle.

ads.title: Made to Be Raised
ads.description: Diageo's Don Julio platform film, directed by Leigh Powis with Thierry Henry arriving at a post-final celebration. Accompanies the new Tequila Don Julio 1942 World Cup 2026 Edition bottle. A second Don Julio film — 'La Otra Copa' (dir. Stillz, with Roberto Carlos + Henry) — runs alongside as the platform's second piece this cycle.

ads.title: For Fans Everywhere
ads.description: Marriott Bonvoy's social-first 2026 platform, anchored on broadcaster Kate Scott and the 'For Fans Everywhere' positioning. Marriott is FIFA's Official Hotel Supporter for North America (Tier 3 Regional Supporter), with the activation spanning 104 matches across the three host countries plus the Marriott Bonvoy Moments hospitality drops. The campaign is published across IG and TikTok with no YouTube canonical — a striking social-first distribution choice for a hospitality brand at this scale, with Vinícius Jr.'s own-channel repost adding talent-amplified reach on top.

ads.title: Some Dreams Start on A Simple Pitch
ads.description: Hisense's 2026 hero spot under its 'Beyond Glory' platform — a generational story positioning football as something that fades from life but never truly leaves. Marks the brand's third consecutive FIFA tournament partnership (eight years across the cycle) and the first hero film from Hisense for the 2026 cycle after a string of regional cutdowns, event content and creator collabs were filtered out during the Hero-focus cleanup.

ads.title: Bandwagon
ads.description: Lay's second tournament chapter, distinct from the 'No Lay's, No Game' watch-party platform — the 'Bandwagon' platform under a 'Jump on, America' frame, inviting fans to ride the tournament with Lay's. Includes a 'From Farm to Field' heritage cutdown tracing the brand's potato fields to the world's biggest stadium. Published on Lay's main @lays handle rather than the dedicated @laysfootball channel that hosts the watch-party work. Builds on Lay's positioning as a long-standing FIFA partner with a multi-platform 2026 cycle (watch-party comedy + bandwagon-rally storytelling running in parallel).

ads.title: Messi Reboot
ads.description: Duracell's 'Built Different' platform with Lionel Messi — a :30 cinematic where Messi runs out of power on generic batteries and is rebooted by the Duracell Scientist's PowerBoost. The activation extends into a limited-edition battery pack printed with Messi's left-leg tattoos (a first for the brand on a partner) and a summer-long sweepstakes. Distribution spans Fox and Telemundo World Cup broadcasts plus YouTube, Amazon and social, with talent amplification via Messi's own Instagram repost ('Duracell — my best kept secret'). Duracell is not a tiered FIFA partner; this is tournament-marketer work positioned around Messi as the GOAT property rather than the World Cup mark itself.
